certified_fingerprint.method: sha256 of each *.go and *.md in the package directory, sorted by FILENAME; then sha256 of that manifest
certified_fingerprint.note: The approval covers this state only. It is the state that ships, so the certified tree and the shipped tree are the same object.

reviews.summary: APPROVE, anchored to package MANIFEST-SHA256 57dc18c1b0277df2 (captured 18:02:10) plus runner.go f35683f3c930e9b8; the approval covers that state only. REVIEWER SELF-CORRECTION: their Round 2 re-raise of the runArm nit was a FALSE POSITIVE -- runArmShuffled landed in v5, the very fingerprint they were certifying, so it was already fixed when reported outstanding. Cause was their grep (searched for `rand.Shuffle` while the call site is `rng.Shuffle` on the *rand.Rand receiver at plugin_test.go:560), not the writer's mtimes; snapshot evidence runArmShuffled count 0 in v1-v4 and 4 in v5-v6. The Round 1 raise was valid since runArmShuffled does not exist in v1-v4. ALSO: the two parties' fingerprints were never in conflict -- the reviewer sorted the manifest by whole line, the writer by filename, so one tree yields 25520e1321b30f70 under theirs and b8c3f7875043cad8 under the writer's; the reviewer's Round 2 anchor and the writer's declared freeze were the SAME tree state. Reviewer has adopted the writer's method. FREEZE PROTOCOL reproduced end to end: all 23 per-file hashes in v6/FINGERPRINT.txt match disk and recomputing the manifest hash from live files gives b8c3f787...cad8 exactly; stating the method for reproduction rather than reverse-engineering was the right call and the per-file manifest is what answered 'what moved' instead of only 'something moved'. BOTH ROUND 1 ISSUES FIXED AND VERIFIED: doc.go:56 now names contract_test.go with no verbatim_test anywhere; runArmShuffled shuffles `scored` from one seeded rand.Rand shared across 60 iterations so the loop samples orderings and failures reproduce, runArm correctly retained for the two tests at :575 and :665 where deterministic input is the point, message reworded to claim only what the harness produces, and the fix verified non-cosmetic -- with the decode sort deleted this test now fails 10/10. MUTATION MATRIX, reproduced on an isolated cp -a at the frozen fingerprint: decode sort removed -> tie-break FAIL 10/10, full-picker FAIL 10/10, cross-product (mirrored) PASS 10/10; prefill sort removed -> tie-break FAIL 10/10, full-picker PASS 8/8 (correct, that fixture has one prefill endpoint). Writer's 10/10 figures hold on both axes; the mirrored cross-product test staying green through a decode-sort deletion is the concrete cost of recomputing an expectation from production's own ordering rule, and the tests are scoped rather than accidentally passing. tAdmD ALGEBRA VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND AGREED: every prefill-endpoint-dependent term feeds remoteLeadUs and is discarded by the max, cXferUs keys off the request, and the surviving tIterFirstDecode and OutputTokenProcessingUs are decode-side only, so J is identical bit-for-bit -- which is why the old map scan was flaky rather than merely fragile. config.go and README write-ups accurate including the P > 1 boundary and the explicit refusal to claim a direction; t.Fatalf over t.Skipf correct because a fixture that stops tying means the overlap no longer behaves as documented. METRIC NAMING closed by the operator as option B, reviewer raising it in neither direction; the parallelism property holds (10 families each, suffixes term-for-term identical after stripping the arm prefix, identical label sets and histogram buckets) so the single-regex cross-arm query works and the writer's correction of the overstated cost is right; TestTheTwoArmsCannotBeInstantiatedTogether correctly asserts the focal arm builds against the same registry SUCCESSFULLY under distinct names, with the comment stating plainly that the collision is not the justification -- the misnomer is, with masking legibility as the secondary gain. generated/leastttftjoint/ RESOLVED and the reviewer judges the writer's reasoning better than their own issue: removing rather than re-syncing is right because the mirror is the main session's later step, all 23 files_created paths resolve in the repo, and a reviewer can no longer reach a different conclusion from the mirror than from the source -- that was the actual defect and it was closed at the root. PROCESS NOTE, not an issue: three files changed after the freeze declaration (config.go, policy_test.go, README.md) and the tree moved twice more during verification (b8c3f787 -> b306bbc9 -> 57dc18c1); reviewer confirmed every .go change comment/blank-only with no production logic file differing from the frozen state, and that they were their own Round 2 recommendations being incorporated, so not blocking -- but it is why the approval names a fingerprint, since otherwise the certified and shipped trees can differ. Verification summary: fidelity (jointCandidateTTFT matches the spec statement-for-statement with only the two mandated adapter substitutions, unconditional math.Max, local omits tIterFirstDecode while disagg adds it, per-side theta, OutputTokenProcessingUs on both projections, plain ascending-ID enumeration with no scorer-first reorder and no Ablation/decomposed branch, verbatim contract verified independently of contract_test.go with four exact copies byte-identical modulo the package clause and all 17 retained function bodies and 5 structs byte-identical with nothing added, focal arm 0 drift across Rounds 1-3); code quality (interfaces confirmed at the pin, PickerFactory errors on nil and wrong-typed handler and inherits the handler's data keys, 149 tests over 10 files including Factory construction, both Round-1 regressions, the pinned both-axes tie-break and two Policy-level race tests, mutation-tested non-vacuous, build/vet/-race/golangci-lint 0 issues, full package 50/50 and -shuffle=on 30/30 in fresh processes, no test deriving an assertion from an unpinned order); registration (both type strings, factories, purely additive runner.go diff with focal lines untouched and handler before picker as backward-only resolution requires); config (overlay format valid, both plugin types registered, producers verified as real registered spellings, zero invented keys, all 12 coefficients exact against inputs/); assembly (scenario name pdinfocomm3 matches, treatment_config_generated true, deep merge simulated -- plugins string replaces the baseline's wholesale so disagg-profile-handler does not survive while epp.replicas:1, pluginsConfigFile, inferenceObjectives, tokenizer sidecar and --enable-force-include-usage all propagate); treatment config (strict subset with every shared key equal to the focal arm's, v/ablation/activeWorkload/workloadTargets/capacity correctly absent, only 1e-12 remaining as a literal and it is the strict-improvement epsilon).

post_verdict_corrections.note: Corrections exchanged AFTER the APPROVE verdict. None changes the verdict or the certified fingerprint; recorded so the audit trail is complete rather than only favourable.
by_reviewer: Issue A's FRAMING was wrong, not merely superseded: the claim that output.json 'lists 23 files_created paths that no longer exist beneath it, so the manifest and the artifact disagree' was faulty, because the manifest never claimed they were beneath it -- the paths are target-repo-relative. Verified 24/24 resolve from the target repo and 0/24 from generated/ for this arm; 26/26 from both for the focal arm, and only because Step 4 had run. There is no manifest defect and there never was. The reviewer's 23/25 counts were files_created only; the writer's 24/26 include files_modified and are the complete manifest.

Issue C was the reviewer's error twice over: fixed before their first raise landed in the state they were certifying, and the re-raise came from grepping `rand.Shuffle` when the call is `rng.Shuffle` on the *rand.Rand receiver at plugin_test.go:560 -- a wrong search pattern, not the stale read the writer had charitably offered.
Issue B asked for a freeze and fingerprint that the Round 3 request already carried. Neither Issue B nor C was a defect in the work and both cost rounds.
The two parties' fingerprints were never in conflict (whole-line sort against filename sort), so the reviewer's Round 2 anchor and the writer's declared freeze were the SAME tree state.

README.md is NOT code-identical across the post-verdict delta (172 -> 206 lines) and that is correct and expected: it is prose, so the stripped-code test does not apply to it. The writer's comment-only claim was scoped to the two .go files and holds exactly there.

The writer's sharpening of the mirrored-test finding is stronger than the reviewer's original: the cross-product fixture's inputs are already in ascending ID order, so the test would be blind to a deleted sort EVEN WITHOUT the sortedByID call in its expectation loop -- two independent causes, either sufficient alone.
by_writer: The Round 3 request described the t.Skipf->t.Fatalf change and the D1 regime note as 'changed since your capture'. Because the two fingerprint methods were incomparable, those changes were in fact already inside the tree the reviewer had certified at Round 2. The account was inaccurate in the direction of over-disclosing rather than under.
post_verdict_corrections.adopted_process_refinement: A freeze means ABORT THE ROUND OR REISSUE THE FINGERPRINT -- never edit under a live certification. Three files moved after the freeze declaration this round and the tree moved twice more during verification (b8c3f787 -> b306bbc9 -> 57dc18c1); the intermediate state b306bbc9 should never have been observable. Only the accident that the changes were documentation-only kept it harmless. Post-verdict edits are to be announced before starting, made atomically, then snapshotted and disclosed.
